title: Dating Photo Reality Check
oneLiner: A playful authenticity booth that helps daters spot over-AI’d profile photos and publish a funny real-human confidence card.
targetUser: Dating-app users, matchmakers, singles communities, safety-conscious daters, and friends reviewing a profile before someone gets embarrassed or catfished.
keyUx: Upload or paste profile photos and prompts; the app highlights too-perfect signals, asks humanizing proof questions, suggests warmer real-photo replacements, and generates a shareable “probably human” card.
searchSignals: Reddit r/ChristianDating — AI-generated dating photos becoming normal: https://www.reddit.com/r/ChristianDating/comments/1sh2ntw/ai_generated_dating_profile_pics_are_becoming_a/
Evie Magazine — AI-generated profiles on dating apps as scam risk: https://www.eviemagazine.com/post/ai-generated-profiles-on-dating-apps-are-the-latest-scam-to-watch-out-for
stitchPrompt: Design a playful mobile-first dating safety prototype called Dating Photo Reality Check for dating-app users, matchmakers, singles communities, safety-conscious daters, and friends reviewing a profile before someone gets embarrassed or catfished. Users should upload or paste profile photos, captions, and conversation openers, then highlight too-perfect AI-photo signals, ask humanizing proof questions, suggest warmer real-photo replacements, estimate catfish embarrassment risk, and generate a shareable probably-human confidence card. Include a profile photo drop zone, too-perfect signal scanner, human proof question deck, catfish embarrassment meter, real-photo replacement coach, friend review reaction strip, and shareable probably-human card. Design direction: use a playful-experimental aesthetic with dating-app swipes, glossy pink/blue gradients, cheeky authenticity stickers, memeable verdict cards, and bold micro-animations so the prototype feels funny, protective, and viral rather than accusatory.
